architecture_summary.operational_context: Cloud-based SaaS integration platform processing webhook events and user-authorized API calls, deployed in multi-tenant Kubernetes environment with managed database services

threat_actors.name: External Opportunistic Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Financial gain via data theft, credential harvesting, or ransomware deployment
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Public webhook endpoint exploitation or stolen OAuth tokens from credential stuffing
non_capabilities: No physical access to cloud infrastructure
No pre-existing insider knowledge of internal topology
Cannot compromise managed database encryption keys

threat_actors.name: Malicious Insider (Compromised Employee)
threat_actors.motivation: Data exfiltration for competitive advantage or sabotage
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate CI/CD pipeline access or internal admin console credentials
non_capabilities: No direct access to external SaaS provider infrastructure
Cannot bypass hardware security module (HSM) protections
No control over external user devices
Cannot modify cloud provider control plane

threat_actors.name: Compromised External SaaS Provider
threat_actors.motivation: Supply chain attack to inject malicious payloads into downstream integrations
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Malicious webhook payloads sent to webhook_receiver
non_capabilities: No direct network access to internal VPC
Cannot forge valid OAuth 2.0 tokens for oauth_proxy
No visibility into internal event queue contents
Cannot directly query integration_db or audit_log

attack_paths.impact: Remote code execution or malicious event injection into event_queue
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Webhook endpoint is publicly exposed; input validation gaps in transformer could allow deserialization attacks

attack_paths.entry_point: OAuth 2.0 token endpoint via stolen refresh tokens
attack_paths.impact: Unauthorized API calls bypassing rate_limiter, accessing downstream integrations
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Credential stuffing and token theft are prevalent; OAuth proxy may lack token binding or device fingerprinting

attack_paths.entry_point: Phishing email directing user to malicious OAuth consent screen
attack_paths.impact: Attacker gains valid OAuth grant for end_user's data via oauth_proxy
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: End users are high-value targets; consent screens can be spoofed if domain validation is weak

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised host in same VPC segment or misconfigured network mirroring
attack_paths.impact: Interception of sensitive event payloads in transit between webhook_receiver/oauth_proxy and event_queue
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Cloud provider network encryption (TLS in transit) mitigates; risk increases with misconfigured VPC flow logs

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious webhook payload exploiting deserialization flaw in transformer
attack_paths.impact: Persistent backdoor in transformer process enabling arbitrary code execution on subsequent events
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Transformer processes untrusted data; lack of sandboxing or strict schema validation enables persistence

attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of all integrated SaaS data stored in integration_db
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Transformer holds DB credentials; if compromised (AP-005), direct data access is trivial

attack_paths.impact: Audit log tampering or deletion to cover tracks of data exfiltration
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Transformer writes audit entries; compromised process can overwrite or delete logs if permissions are excessive

attack_paths.entry_point: High-volume request flood from external_saas or end_user
attack_paths.impact: Rate limiter exhaustion causing legitimate webhook/OAuth traffic to be dropped
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Rate limiter is a choke point; distributed flood from compromised SaaS or botnet can overwhelm fixed limits

mitigations.control_name: Immutable Audit Logs with WORM Storage

findings.severity_rationale: Public webhook endpoint with insufficient input validation allows RCE via deserialization, leading to full pipeline compromise
Stolen OAuth tokens grant full API access without additional verification; token binding and device fingerprinting not implemented
Spearphishing can trick users into granting malicious OAuth consent; domain validation and user education gaps exist
Network sniffing risk mitigated by cloud provider TLS; residual risk only from misconfiguration
Transformer compromise leads to direct database access and audit log tampering; no runtime protection or least-privilege DB credentials
Rate limiter is single point of failure for DoS; adaptive limits and upstream DDoS protection partially deployed

agentic.blast_radius: No autonomous agents in architecture; all components are deterministic services
human_oversight_points: All deployment changes require human approval via CI/CD gates
Database schema changes require DBA review
